one_line_pitch: Non-invasive EEG-based cognitive monitoring patch for early Alzheimer's detection in primary care.
problem_statement: Alzheimer's disease is typically diagnosed 7-10 years after neurological changes begin. Primary care physicians lack accessible, low-cost tools for early cognitive screening. Existing diagnostics require specialist referrals and expensive imaging.
proposed_solution: A wearable EEG patch worn for 30 minutes during a routine GP visit. Our proprietary signal processing algorithm identifies early-stage biomarkers associated with cognitive decline. Integrates with EHR systems via HL7 FHIR API.
target_market: Primary care physicians in the US and UK. Target is 150,000 GP practices. Broader addressable market includes neurology clinics and memory care centres.
business_model: Device lease model: $200/month per practice includes device, disposable patches, and software platform. Reimbursement pathway via CPT code 95999 (EEG analysis).
traction_summary: NHS pilot with 3 GP practices in Manchester. 47 patient assessments completed. 91% clinician satisfaction. Regulatory pre-submission meeting with MHRA completed. NIH SBIR Phase I award of $250,000 received.
competitive_landscape: Alzheimer's Research UK reports no FDA/MHRA-cleared EEG-based screening device currently in GP settings. Nearest competitors are specialist neuroimaging (PET/MRI) and blood biomarker tests (Lumipulse, not yet widely reimbursed).
technical_status: CE Mark application submitted. FDA Breakthrough Device Designation application in preparation. Clinical algorithm validated on 340-patient dataset (90% sensitivity, 87% specificity). EHR integration built on FHIR R4.
supporting_documents: NIH SBIR Phase I award notification
